:::{#thm-taylor-1d}
#### Taylor's theorem with a second-order remainder

Let $a < b$, and let $g$ be a real-valued function on $[a, b]$
whose derivative $g'$ is [continuous](calculus.qmd#def-continuous) on $[a, b]$
and whose [second derivative](calculus.qmd#def-second-derivative) $g''$ exists at every point of $(a, b)$.
Then there is a $\midpt \in (a, b)$ with
[@wikipedia_taylors_theorem]

$$
g(b) = g(a) + g'(a)\,(b - a) + \frac{1}{2}\,g''(\midpt)\,(b - a)^2.
$$

:::

This is the case $n = 2$ of [@rudin1976principles, Theorem 5.15].
